findings.fix: Replace the code or jargon term with a plain-language sentence a non-technical reader can act on.
findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.violation: The message text carries an internal error code, a code-style token, or an engineering-jargon term standing in for a plain-language explanation.

findings.fix: Add an acknowledgment: briefly restate what happened in plain terms and what the reader can do next (retry, contact support).
findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.violation: A total failure (error 502, reader cannot proceed) is reported as a bare technical notice with no acknowledgment of what this means to the reader.

findings.fix: Add acknowledgment and tone: 'We're sorry - your recent changes couldn't be saved. We've contacted our team to investigate. In the meantime, contact support for help.'
findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.violation: A total failure (unrecoverable data loss) is reported as a bare technical notice with no acknowledgment of what data loss means to the reader or sincere tone.

findings.fix: Add file-type validation at file-picker time: show a warning or restrict selectable file types to PDF and PNG before submission.
findings.evidence: Receipts upload as PDF or PNG only, the two formats the expense system can read. Change this file to one of those formats and upload it again, or select a different receipt.
findings.violation: A foreseeable format restriction (Predictable mistake=yes) is reported only after form submission (Fires=on-submit), though the product could have warned during file selection.

findings.fix: Place this message directly above or inline with the password field, not at the top of the form.
findings.evidence: Placement: at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page
findings.violation: The message sits at the top of a form while the field it concerns is lower down, requiring scrolling away from the field to read the message.

findings.fix: Use a modal dialog container instead of a toast, or keep a persistent inline message until the reader dismisses it explicitly.
findings.evidence: Container: toast; Placement: 'in a dialog centered on the password reset step, over the new password field it blocks'
findings.violation: A blocking failure (reset link expired, reader cannot proceed with password reset) is shown in a toast that clears itself, so a reader who looks away misses the only message explaining why the field is blocked.

findings.fix: Offer a one-click 'Compress and retry' action instead of only describing manual compression steps.
findings.evidence: Suggested fix: described, names the one available alternative but requires the reader to enter it by hand
findings.violation: The fix (reduce file size) is unambiguous and single but only described in prose, requiring the reader to manually perform the compression outside the product.

findings.fix: Specify which changes failed to save and why: 'Your username change couldn't be saved due to a connection error. Your email address was updated successfully.'
findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered.
findings.violation: The message reports 'changes' without naming which fields were changed or why the save failed, leaving the reader with no understanding of what was lost.
